Department of Architecture

Guidelines for PhD Qualifying Examinations (QE)
Approval Date: 20 March 2025

1. INTRODUCTION
The PhD Qualifying Examinations (QE) are a key milestone to conﬁrm the candidature of
PhD students within NUS. According to CDE policies, the QE “comprises a
comprehensive written examination (CQE) followed by an Oral Qualifying Examination
(OQE) of the PhD thesis proposal. The CQE is to test the general competence of the
candidate in his/her discipline(s), while the OQE ensures that the candidate is prepared
to embark on his/her thesis research. 1”
The following document provides disciplinary speciﬁc guidelines for PhD students in the
Department of Architecture (DoA) to supplement CDE policies and ensure parity across
the department.
These guidelines are effective for PhD students admitted from AY 2025/26 onwards. For
students enrolled prior to AY2025/26, the thesis advisors have discretion to adjust the
content of the exam as outlined in Section 5 PhD Thesis Proposal.
2. ELIGIBILITY & EVALUATION OF QE
Students must complete all required coursework as outlined in the CDE Research
Student Handbook prior to the Oral Qualifying Exam (OQE).
In accordance with CDE guidelines, PhD students in DoA will complete the two
components of the QE process in sequence—the CQE and OQE. Students must pass
the CQE prior to completing the OQE for candidacy, but the ﬁnal evaluation will
consider both components together in the ﬁnal report. It is possible for a student to fail
one or both components of the QE in their ﬁrst attempt. The Thesis Advisory Committee
(TAC) will determine the outcome once they are satisﬁed that the student has passed
both components of the QE.
3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
PhD Student
Students are responsible for managing their own research and professional
development. They should maintain frequent and regular contact with their thesis
advisor(s) and take initiative, in consultation with their advisor(s), to form a thesis
advisory committee (TAC). Students are also responsible to coordinate and schedule
necessary milestones related to the QE process.

5. PHD THESIS PROPOSAL
DoA students will submit one document with three components prior to the
commencement of the QE process. This includes: (1) Research Statement (2) Thesis
Research Proposal and (3) Extended Bibliography. Each of these components shall be
drafted on A4 pages using 11-point font. Speciﬁc requirements are as follows:
(1) Research Statement (3-5 pages)
Students will contextualize their trajectory as a researcher by identifying their
disciplinary expertise. The student should consult their thesis advisor(s) about the
appropriate approach to describing their expertise. This can be done by identifying a
major ﬁeld and minor ﬁeld of study. The major ﬁeld typically is a subﬁeld that aligns
with the students’ academic discipline (e.g. architecture, architecture/urban history,
landscape architecture, urban planning, urban design, or others), and the minor
ﬁelds reﬂect the speciﬁc research interests of the student relevant to their research.
The Research Statement should include, but is not limited to, the following:
a. Contextualize and describe the major and minor ﬁelds of study within your
research trajectory, and the student’s position within these ﬁelds of
knowledge
b. Outline relevant coursework or professional experiences that contribute to
your expertise in these ﬁelds of knowledge
(2) Thesis Research Proposal (maximum 30 pages)

their proposed thesis project. Students should discuss with their thesis advisor(s)

(3) Extended Bibliography (No page limit)
The extended bibliography expands the reference list of the thesis research proposal by
including additional literature relevant to the student’s disciplinary expertise and ﬁelds
of study. Students will organize the bibliography in sections that demonstrate their
knowledge in their chosen ﬁelds of expertise, and consider content related to the
theoretical and historical development of their ﬁelds, methodological approaches, and
current discourses or debates. Each section should include a brief paragraph describing
the literature listed.
Students will consult with their TAC about the appropriate content and length of this
bibliography. Typical bibliographies for the humanities and social science include
approximately 100 books. This extended bibliography is the basis for the CQE exam, and
students are encouraged to include 3-5 sample questions that illustrate the topics they
are prepared to answer in the written exam.
The extended bibliography should include the following:
a. Brief description of each ﬁeld of expertise
b. Selected bibliography organized in appropriate subsections
c. 3-5 Sample Questions
6. FORMAT OF EXAMINATION
Comprehensive Written Examination (CQE)
The CQE assesses the general competence and disciplinary knowledge of PhD students
in their chosen ﬁelds. It also allows the TAC to evaluate key research components, such
as research impact, literature review, research methods, and proposed deliverables. It is
a “take-home” exam comprising of questions determined by the TAC. Speciﬁc
requirements are as follows:
Duration: Five Days, students can submit their answers earlier
Total number of questions on the paper: Three to six.
Number of questions to be answered: Three.

 Form of Answers: Each answer will not exceed 2000 words, excluding
references, images, and tables. Answers should combine evidence of depth of
understanding and awareness of broader contexts of their chosen ﬁelds.
Answers should be typed and submitted in a single *.docx or *.pdf ﬁle, 11-point
font.
Any deviations from this format should be approved prior to the submission of the PhD
Research Proposal by the PhD Ad-Hoc Committee. The TAC should agree on the
questions forming the CQE before submission to the department. The questions will be
sent to students via email at 9am on the ﬁrst day of their exam.
Oral Qualifying Examination (OQE)
The OQE will be open to the academic community at NUS and any relevant individuals
involved in the thesis project. During the two-hour OQE, students will present their
research proposal for 30 minutes followed by Q&A from the TAC and members of the
audience.
At the request of the TAC, a closed-door Q&A session with the student may commence
after the public presentation to clarify issues related to the CQE or other sensitive
issues. The TAC and thesis advisor(s) will convene in a closed-door session to discuss
and evaluate the student’s CQE and OQE. The TAC and thesis advisor(s) will then invite
the student back into the room and inform them of the ﬁnal outcome of the QE at the
end of the session.

Tuesday, 9am – 12pm, 12pm – 2pm, SR8
The course introduces students to ways of looking at and
discussing works of art. The focus is chiefly on painting and
sculpture; the emphasis is on analysing the composition or
design of art works and in constructing meanings for them.
The study of this course enables students to acquire critical
skills for interpreting and connecting with works of art. The
course encourages students to read art works in relation to
a range of interests, intentions and issues; the aim here is

Department of Architecture

Guidelines for PhD Qualifying Examinations (QE)
Approval Date: 20 March 2025

1. INTRODUCTION
The PhD Qualifying Examinations (QE) are a key milestone to conﬁrm the candidature of
PhD students within NUS. According to CDE policies, the QE “comprises a
comprehensive written examination (CQE) followed by an Oral Qualifying Examination
(OQE) of the PhD thesis proposal. The CQE is to test the general competence of the
candidate in his/her discipline(s), while the OQE ensures that the candidate is prepared
to embark on his/her thesis research. 1”
The following document provides disciplinary speciﬁc guidelines for PhD students in the
Department of Architecture (DoA) to supplement CDE policies and ensure parity across
the department.
These guidelines are effective for PhD students admitted from AY 2025/26 onwards. For
students enrolled prior to AY2025/26, the thesis advisors have discretion to adjust the
content of the exam as outlined in Section 5 PhD Thesis Proposal.
2. ELIGIBILITY & EVALUATION OF QE
Students must complete all required coursework as outlined in the CDE Research
Student Handbook prior to the Oral Qualifying Exam (OQE).
In accordance with CDE guidelines, PhD students in DoA will complete the two
components of the QE process in sequence—the CQE and OQE. Students must pass
the CQE prior to completing the OQE for candidacy, but the ﬁnal evaluation will
consider both components together in the ﬁnal report. It is possible for a student to fail
one or both components of the QE in their ﬁrst attempt. The Thesis Advisory Committee
(TAC) will determine the outcome once they are satisﬁed that the student has passed
both components of the QE.
3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
PhD Student
Students are responsible for managing their own research and professional
development. They should maintain frequent and regular contact with their thesis
advisor(s) and take initiative, in consultation with their advisor(s), to form a thesis
advisory committee (TAC). Students are also responsible to coordinate and schedule
necessary milestones related to the QE process.
Thesis Advisor(s)
Each student will have a main thesis supervisor and can have up to two additional cothesis advisors. The main thesis advisor must be a full-time faculty member (e.g. Senior
1

https://cde.nus.edu.sg/graduate/graduate-programmes-by-research/programme-structure-2/

 Lecturers, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor) in the Department of
Architecture. The thesis advisor(s) will advise student on necessary coursework and
supervise preparation of the QE proposal, and later completion of the thesis.
The main thesis advisor is responsible for coordinating with other members of the TAC
throughout the QE process, including but not limited to collecting CQE questions,
coordinating necessary reports, and liaising with department administrators.
Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC)
There should be a minimum of three members of the Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC),
including the thesis advisors. The composition of the TAC is as follows:
-

Minimum 1 member should be full-time faculty in DoA that is not the main thesis
advisor
Other members should be full-time faculty in NUS or other universities that are
familiar with the subject matter proposed by the student.

The TAC is responsible for evaluating the overall QE process, setting exam questions for
the CQE, and questioning during the OQE.
The OQE is chaired by the Exam Committee Chair, who also endorses and composes
the evaluation report. The Exam Committee Chair must be a Senior faculty (Associate
Professor and above) in DoA and is conﬁrmed/appointed by the Deputy Head of
Research. They may also be a part of the TAC.
Members of the TAC, who are not thesis advisors, must declare any conﬂict of interest,
including any co-authorship or membership in the same research group/grant. Previous
instructors are acceptable, and we encourage PhD students to actively take courses
with potential TAC members. The ﬁnal composition of the TAC will be approved by the
Deputy Head of Research.
Deputy Head of Research
The Deputy Head of Research is responsible for approving the ﬁnal composition of the
TAC and appointing the Exam Chair.
4. TIMELINE
CDE requires that PhD students should complete their QE, including both the written
CQE and oral OQE, within 24 months of enrolment in the PhD programme. To comply
with these guidelines, DoA recommends that students consider attempting their QE
beginning in their 18th-20th month of enrolment, and any second attempt—if the ﬁrst
attempt results in failure—should be scheduled within two months.
A recommended timeline for PhD students in DoA is as follows:
Six to Eight months prior to CQE: Students should deﬁne the scope of their CQE and
thesis research, and approach potential faculty to form their TAC.
Three months prior to CQE: Students should ﬁnalize the TAC and submit draft QE
proposal, which includes a reading list and thesis proposal, to members of the TAC.

 Members of the TAC should provide constructive feedback to the students for revisions.
The ﬁnal proposal must be approved by the Thesis advisor before submitting to the
department.
4 weeks prior to CQE: Student to submit ﬁnal proposal to the Department and TAC. The
thesis advisor(s) will coordinate with the TAC to compose CQE questions.
1 week prior to CQE: TAC to submit exam questions to DH (Research) or designated
representative for approval
Comprehensive Written Exam (CQE): take home written exam
1 week after CQE: the TAC to Indicate whether the student is recommended to proceed
to the OQE.
1 to 3 weeks after the TAC recommendation: the OQE to be scheduled.
1 week prior to the OQE: Department administrator will solicit abstract and title of
thesis proposal and send an invitation to the DoA community to attend the OQE.
Oral Qualiﬁcation Exam (OQE): two-hour block, including time for TAC to deliberate
5. PHD THESIS PROPOSAL
DoA students will submit one document with three components prior to the
commencement of the QE process. This includes: (1) Research Statement (2) Thesis
Research Proposal and (3) Extended Bibliography. Each of these components shall be
drafted on A4 pages using 11-point font. Speciﬁc requirements are as follows:
(1) Research Statement (3-5 pages)
Students will contextualize their trajectory as a researcher by identifying their
disciplinary expertise. The student should consult their thesis advisor(s) about the
appropriate approach to describing their expertise. This can be done by identifying a
major ﬁeld and minor ﬁeld of study. The major ﬁeld typically is a subﬁeld that aligns
with the students’ academic discipline (e.g. architecture, architecture/urban history,
landscape architecture, urban planning, urban design, or others), and the minor
ﬁelds reﬂect the speciﬁc research interests of the student relevant to their research.
The Research Statement should include, but is not limited to, the following:
a. Contextualize and describe the major and minor ﬁelds of study within your
research trajectory, and the student’s position within these ﬁelds of
knowledge
b. Outline relevant coursework or professional experiences that contribute to
your expertise in these ﬁelds of knowledge
(2) Thesis Research Proposal (maximum 30 pages)
The OQE examines whether the PhD student is sufficiently prepared to embark on
their proposed thesis project. Students should discuss with their thesis advisor(s)
about the appropriate scope of the proposal. Students should consult their

 advisor(s) about the appropriate format of the research proposal, but it should be
concise and may include the following:
a.
b.
c.
d.
e.
f.
g.
h.
i.

Abstract
Introduction
Research Questions
Background & Literature Review
Signiﬁcance & Contribution
Methodology
Preliminary ﬁndings
Thesis Chapter Outlines
Work Plan

(3) Extended Bibliography (No page limit)
The extended bibliography expands the reference list of the thesis research proposal by
including additional literature relevant to the student’s disciplinary expertise and ﬁelds
of study. Students will organize the bibliography in sections that demonstrate their
knowledge in their chosen ﬁelds of expertise, and consider content related to the
theoretical and historical development of their ﬁelds, methodological approaches, and
current discourses or debates. Each section should include a brief paragraph describing
the literature listed.
Students will consult with their TAC about the appropriate content and length of this
bibliography. Typical bibliographies for the humanities and social science include
approximately 100 books. This extended bibliography is the basis for the CQE exam, and
students are encouraged to include 3-5 sample questions that illustrate the topics they
are prepared to answer in the written exam.
The extended bibliography should include the following:
a. Brief description of each ﬁeld of expertise
b. Selected bibliography organized in appropriate subsections
c. 3-5 Sample Questions
6. FORMAT OF EXAMINATION
Comprehensive Written Examination (CQE)
The CQE assesses the general competence and disciplinary knowledge of PhD students
in their chosen ﬁelds. It also allows the TAC to evaluate key research components, such
as research impact, literature review, research methods, and proposed deliverables. It is
a “take-home” exam comprising of questions determined by the TAC. Speciﬁc
requirements are as follows:
Duration: Five Days, students can submit their answers earlier
Total number of questions on the paper: Three to six.
Number of questions to be answered: Three.

 Form of Answers: Each answer will not exceed 2000 words, excluding
references, images, and tables. Answers should combine evidence of depth of
understanding and awareness of broader contexts of their chosen ﬁelds.
Answers should be typed and submitted in a single *.docx or *.pdf ﬁle, 11-point
font.
Any deviations from this format should be approved prior to the submission of the PhD
Research Proposal by the PhD Ad-Hoc Committee. The TAC should agree on the
questions forming the CQE before submission to the department. The questions will be
sent to students via email at 9am on the ﬁrst day of their exam.
Oral Qualifying Examination (OQE)
The OQE will be open to the academic community at NUS and any relevant individuals
involved in the thesis project. During the two-hour OQE, students will present their
research proposal for 30 minutes followed by Q&A from the TAC and members of the
audience.
At the request of the TAC, a closed-door Q&A session with the student may commence
after the public presentation to clarify issues related to the CQE or other sensitive
issues. The TAC and thesis advisor(s) will convene in a closed-door session to discuss
and evaluate the student’s CQE and OQE. The TAC and thesis advisor(s) will then invite
the student back into the room and inform them of the ﬁnal outcome of the QE at the
end of the session.

|------|------|

|------|------|

| 公开性 | 向 NUS 学术社区开放 |

| 后续 | 可能进行 closed-door Q&A（TAC 视需要） |
| 评估 | TAC + thesis advisor(s) closed-door 讨论后，当场告知结果 |

### 四、推荐时间线

### 五、TAC 组成
- 最少 **3 人**（含 thesis advisor）
- 至少 1 人必须是 **DoA 全职 faculty**（非 main thesis advisor）
- 其他成员可以是 NUS 或其他大学熟悉你研究主题的全职 faculty
- Exam Chair 必须是 DoA **Associate Professor 及以上**，由 Deputy Head of Research 任命

---

所以你记忆中的 **100 本书 + annotated bibliography** 是对的，就是 Extended Bibliography 部分——约 100 本书，按主题分节，每节附一段简要描述，并附 3-5 个 sample questions。
